checks.rationale: TASK-007-AC1 exact-root/HEAD observation and AC2 developer preservation fail in three actual Windows/Linux probes (findings 001-003).
Scope and exclusions remain bounded, but the implemented REQ-02/AC-02 safety slice permits movement of a checked-out developer branch and writes after managed checkout identity changes.

Source traces connect string-only checkout matching with dereferencing publication, before-state classification without the required HEAD match, and the missing-HEAD root-proof bypass to three observed defects.

The changed managed checkout receives read-tree writes before the adapter returns unknown; error reporting does not preserve its existing index/files (finding 002). Lost-command reconciliation otherwise remains conservative.
Actual symbolic target, managed branch-switch and false missing-HEAD boundaries are not handled safely, despite existing coverage of ordinary states, NUL paths, stale refs and dirty/index races.

The meaningful declared 29-test suite independently passes on Windows (one filename skip); bound minimum-version/Linux evidence also passes. The three required regressions independently reproduced on both hosts are absent.
Only the Git adapter, its leaf tests and owned handoff change. The finite helper and local bindings require no new frozen DTO, downstream service, stdin/checkpoint port or ignored runtime helper.

Raw Git diff contains exactly the three declared additions. Candidate is clean, base/dependencies are ancestors, owner-final bytes match, all manifest hashes and graph/isolation structural digests recompute.

Explicit accepted local_ports interfaces, injected collaborators and a closed helper within the tracked flat module preserve the architecture and runtime closure. No unnecessary alternative abstraction was found.

Fixed argv, complete digest-checked evidence and trusted-runtime shadow resistance pass, but symbolic target redirection and lost checkout admission violate the developer preservation boundary (findings 001-002). Native rank-4 reviewer selection is separate from rank-3 implementation; unavailable provider-effective identity/effort is explicitly disclosed.

The handoff describes the implemented mechanisms and limitations, but its claims of exact-root proof and preservation of developer branches/index/files are contradicted by the three actual reproductions.

findings.description: A symbolic target refs/heads/alias -> refs/heads/main bypasses checkout protection because _checked_out_paths (line 698) compares the alias string, while update-ref --stdin (line 1354) dereferences it. With main checked out, an expected-present branch request using a newer source returns succeeded/changed=true and moves developer main, leaving its old index as staged deletions. Reproduced with actual Git on Windows and Linux.
findings.expected_fix: Observe and constrain symbolic target identity. Reject symbolic mutation targets explicitly or safely resolve/guard their referents and apply checkout policy to the actual ref, including alias retargeting. Add an actual-repository regression preserving developer HEAD, index and files; update the handoff.

findings.description: After managed integration publication, ordinary git checkout developer leaves a clean old tree under a different branch. _managed_after_state (lines 608-609) still returns before despite the observed HEAD mismatch; its caller (line 542) invokes read-tree and adds candidate.txt to the developer files/index before returning unknown/changed=None. Reproduced on both hosts; read_tree_calls=1 and index_preserved=false.
findings.expected_fix: Treat the observed HEAD/branch mismatch as unresolved without advancing the checkout. Revalidate the admitted branch, binding and sole checkout, expected published HEAD, old index and worktree before permitting read-tree. Add the actual branch-switch regression and retain existing dirty/index preservation tests; update the handoff.

findings.description: The missing-HEAD shortcut (lines 239-253) skips exact-root proof for any .git directory lacking HEAD, then ignores successful HEAD resolution. An ordinary nested directory containing an empty .git yields succeeded, HEAD missing and enclosing refs/heads/main present, even though Git resolves the enclosing repository and its present HEAD. Reproduced on Windows and Linux.
findings.expected_fix: Prove that missing-HEAD metadata belongs to the exact bound root, reject parent-repository fallback and contradictory successful HEAD resolution, and retain legitimate missing-HEAD support. Add the actual nested empty-.git regression and update the handoff.
